scenes.headline: Creation and the Creator
visual: The field, and the one who knows it
scenes.say: Chapter Thirteen. Creation and the Creator. Krishna now separates two things we usually mix up: the body, and the one who knows it.
In many translations this is called the field and the knower of the field. Our book uses the words creation and creator. Verse one. {verse}
And Krishna says where real knowledge lies. Verse two. {verse}

scenes.headline: What the field is made of
visual: Nature, intellect, ego, the five elements
The ten organs, the mind, the sense objects
Desire, hatred, pleasure, pain
scenes.say: He lists what belongs to the creation, the field: primal nature, the cosmic intellect, the ego, the five elements, the ten organs, the mind, and the five objects of the senses. And then, surprisingly, he adds desire, hatred, pleasure and pain. Even our feelings are part of the field. The one who knows them is not.
Then Krishna gives a remarkable definition of knowledge. It is not a list of facts. It is a list of qualities. {verse}

scenes.headline: Hands and eyes everywhere
visual: His hands, feet and eyes are everywhere
Inside and outside all beings
Very far away, and very near
scenes.say: Krishna then describes the Supreme the only way it can be described: in paradox. His hands and feet, his eyes, heads and mouths are everywhere. He perceives without senses, sustains all without being attached. He is inside and outside all beings, moving and unmoving. He is too subtle to grasp, and so he is very far away, and very near.
Why, then, are we born again and again? Verse twenty-one. {verse}
And what does true sight look like? Verse twenty-seven. {verse}

scenes.headline: Space is never stained
visual: As space is not tainted by what fills it
So the Spirit is not tainted by the body
As one sun lights the whole world
scenes.say: Krishna ends with two images. Just as all-pervading space is never stained by what moves within it, the Spirit dwelling in every body is never stained. And just as one sun lights up the whole world, the one Spirit lights up the whole of creation.

visual: The body, mind, ego and senses: the field
The eternal Spirit: the knower
Wisdom begins by telling them apart
scenes.say: Lesson one. The body is the field; the soul is the knower of the field. The body, with its mind, ego, senses and everything they meet, is the field. The eternal Spirit that perceives it is the knower. Wisdom begins by telling the two apart.

visual: Humility, nonviolence, forgiveness, honesty
Purity, steadiness, self-control
Knowledge is a way of being
scenes.say: Lesson two. True knowledge is marked by humility and spiritual virtues. Real knowledge is not information. It is a way of being: humble, honest, nonviolent, forgiving, pure, steady and self-controlled, devoted, and calm in good times and bad.

visual: No fixed form, yet perceiving through all
Inside and outside every being
Described only by paradox
scenes.say: Lesson three. God is everywhere, yet beyond all description. He has no fixed form, yet perceives through every sense. He enjoys the modes of nature without being bound by them, and is at once inside and outside all beings. Words can only point.

visual: Matter and Spirit are both beginningless
Attachment to the gunas causes birth
Good and bad births follow from it
scenes.say: Lesson four. Nature and Spirit are both beginningless. Matter and consciousness both have no beginning. The body comes from nature; the experience of pleasure and pain comes from the soul's association with it. And the soul's attachment to the modes of nature is what causes birth, in good wombs and bad.

visual: The same Lord dwells equally in all
Whoever sees this harms no one
And reaches the supreme abode
scenes.say: Lesson five. Perceiving God equally in all beings is the highest vision. Whoever sees the same eternal Lord in every mortal being truly sees. And because they see it, they injure no one, and they reach the highest.

scenes.headline: Five paths to freedom
visual: Selfless service
Knowledge
Devotion
Meditation
Surrender
scenes.say: Lesson six. Liberation is available through five paths. The soul can be freed through selfless service, through self-knowledge, through devotion, through meditation, or through surrender. All five lead to the same goal. Choose the one that fits your nature, and some, Krishna says, reach it simply by faith.

scenes.headline: Know the knower
visual: The body is the field; you are its knower
Knowledge is humility and virtue
See the same Lord in everyone
scenes.say: So, Chapter Thirteen. The body, the mind and even our feelings are the field. We are the one who knows it. Knowledge shows itself as humility and virtue, and true sight sees the same Lord in everyone. Next, Krishna explains the three forces that bind us to the field.
